problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+x{y}^{′}+y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y(x)={c}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+{c}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x),
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+x{y}^{′}+y=0,\,y(1)=2,\,{y}^{′}(1)=-5,\,x>0.
$$
worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- Substituting $y(1)=2$ into the general solution gives

$$
2={c}_{1}.
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=-5,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={x}^{-1}({c}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-{c}_{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute ${y}^{′}(1)=-5$ and ${c}_{1}=2$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-5 & ={c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y(x)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x).
$$
